newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn called down one to two cents on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn called down one to two cents on weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were expected to open one to two cents per bushel lower, mostly in response to favorable growing weather in the Corn Belt, traders said.
"Corn is going to be a little easier, but it's more weather than anything else," said one floor trader.
Rain has been forecast for much of the western Midwest this weekend, while lesser amounts were seen in the eastern Midwest over the weekend, according to a forecast from Weather Express.
Temperatures are expected to hover around normal levels and do not pose any threat to the corn crop, traders said.
Adjustments in corn supply and demand data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture were as expected and seen as largely neutral for futures, traders said.
In overnight trade, corn futures were 1/4 to 1-1/4 cents lower, with September down 1/4 at $2.34-1/4.
